reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: Reconstructed the English Ancient History route directly from joint OER Articles 9–14 and the dated course table, checked the four redirected VU descriptions and actual entry rules, then reconsidered each UCR course contribution and comparator placement against the frozen record. This separate analytical pass was by the same AI, not an independent person.
findings: The joint degree requires a specialisation. The original generic restricted-choice placeholders did not establish one valid route. The current joint regulations list Ancient History first and specify its five courses. The English orientation list permits Classical Mythology and Seminar Ancient History. These follow the shared first-year surveys; the seminar explicitly serves BA1 Ancient Studies and its prior-history condition is met.

Each year contains sixty unique credits. The first two years are completed before the thesis, which includes its colloquium. The positive-BSA rule and forty-eight-credit threshold are explicit in the joint OER. Open space remains thirty EC, with no more than twelve EC placement and the prescribed outside-programme and introductory-level limits. Practical exercises have the eighty-five percent participation rule. Non-credit literacy, orientation and tutoring are separately recorded.

The specialist courses include Near Eastern history without Akkadian for this route, Roman decline, political relations, ancient masses and contested world heritage. The redirected VU descriptions clarify their content. The generic MKDA reference on World Heritage points to programme-year progression rather than a named subject prerequisite; the joint Ancient Studies OER itself prescribes this course and its progression. No unrelated MKDA course is invented as a prerequisite.

The closest UCR response has substantial ancient textual and material study. The two additional options make different curricular choices in museum and public-history inquiry or political thought and comparison. Later-period courses have specific interpretive, critical or methodological roles. Removed school rhetoric, modern TV and some generic modern legal work when they did not strongly support the intended concept. All three complete curricula satisfy formal workbook constraints and the pairwise distinctness floor.

Reconsidered thirteen positive alignments from the actual sources: scope differences do not prohibit a meaningful relationship in material interpretation, literature, myth, philosophy, ancient politics, empire, humanities methodology, canon formation, creative writing or contested heritage. Specialist sources, religion, Near Eastern depth, excursion, open electives and thesis retain appropriate blanks. Read twenty-five external labels, six note anchors, three concepts and thirty-eight selected UCR descriptions using the established audience and renderer mapping.
